references.text: The frogs come up and cover Egypt, a parallel description of the same plague.
Describes how the frogs came up all over Egypt, including over the people, fulfilling the warning.
The psalmist remembers how God sent frogs that destroyed the Egyptians.
Refers to the frog plague where their land swarmed with frogs, even in the king's bedroom.
Unclean spirits like frogs come out of the mouth of the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet, an allusion to Egypt's frog plague.
Direct continuation of the same plague event; shows God's control over removing the judgment.
Theological contrast between the order of creation (dominion over creeping things) and the chaos of judgment (invasion by creeping things).
